subject: Renewal pricing — lock & flexible ramp proposal
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@cloudcraft.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: pricing concerns and options

Hi Logan,

We’re starting renewal planning for CloudCraft — our current term ends 2027-08-15 — and finance flagged potential material rate increases in your pricing band for next year. We’d like to explore options to lock predictable pricing while keeping some flexibility for our ramp.

Attached is our internal usage forecast for the next 24 months (CloudCraft_Renewal_Forecast.xlsx). High level asks:
- Can Redwood provide a multi-year pricing guarantee to avoid any surprise unit-cost increases?
- We prefer a payment structure that smooths cash flow (annual prepay or staggered prepay) but need capability to scale down/up within reason.
- Any concessions for a 36-month commitment vs 12-month?

Can you propose a couple of structures (e.g., multi-year lock with annual reconciliation, or staged prepay with true-ups)? We’ll loop procurement/legal when we have a term sheet.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Cloud Platform
CloudCraft Inc.

---
Attachment: CloudCraft_Renewal_Forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@cloudcraft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing concerns and options

Hi Elena — thanks for the forecast and the clear asks. Put together a short outline below and attached a starter term sheet (LockAndFlex_TermSheet_v1.pdf). High level proposals we can run for CloudCraft:

Option A — Price Lock + Annual Prepay (Conservative)
- 36-month fixed unit price (locks current band)
- Annual prepay (pay each year up front at a 7% discount vs monthly)
- Annual reconciliation true-up based on actuals; no refunds but credits applied to following year if you overprepay

Option B — Lock & Flex (Preferred for growth)
- 36-month capped unit price (cap guarantees you’ll never pay above X)
- Staged prepay: 40% upfront year 1, 30% year 2, 30% year 3 (can be converted to quarterly draws)
- Quarterly/annual true-ups with potential partial refund if usage substantially under-indexes (<60% of committed)
- Built-in ramp credits: first-year ramp credit of 25% on incremental usage above the baseline to offset onboarding burst

Option C — Multi-year Commitment with Quarterly True-up (Finance-friendly)
- 24–36 month term options with tiered discounts tied to committed monthly throughput
- Quarterly reconciliation and option to buydown remaining commitment if growth pauses

Questions:
1) Which structure is most important to CloudCraft: absolute cash predictability (prepay) or price cap flexibility?
2) How aggressive is the expected ramp vs your forecast file? The term sheet assumes year 1 baseline = Q3 2027 forecast numbers.

If you prefer, we can model three price points and a blended payment schedule for procurement. Couple us in on your legal/procurement timeline and we’ll prepare a more formal commercial term sheet.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: LockAndFlex_TermSheet_v1.pdf (term sheet, 2 pages)
From: Elena Park <elena@cloudcraft.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudCraft Finance <finance@cloudcraft.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing concerns and options

Logan — this is really helpful. A few clarifications from procurement/finance:
- Finance prefers annual prepay vs quarterly to minimize admin, but they’re open to staged prepay if there’s a clear refund/credit mechanism.
- We need a contractual cap on unit price (so our budgeting team can forecast).
- Refund mechanics are a sticking point — finance wants at least a partial refund if actuals are <50% of committed over a 12-month window.

Operational ask: can you support a mid-year true-up (not just annual) so we don’t get too far out of sync? Also, can you include a short blackout calendar for burst events so our SRE team knows the ramp credit applies to organic growth only (not temporary test spikes)?

If you can produce a revised term sheet that reflects: cap on unit price, annual prepay with mid-year true-up option, and partial refund band for sustained underuse, we’ll circulate to legal.

Thanks — looping in finance now.
Elena

---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing concerns and options

Logan / team — I reviewed the forecast and Elena’s asks. We can accommodate a capped unit price plus more flexible refund mechanics, but need guardrails:

- Cap model: set a year-over-year cap that increases at a fixed CPI floor (0%) to protect both sides. The cap should be expressed as a per-token/per-inference unit ceiling.
- Refund band: allow a partial refund if actual annualized usage <50% of committed for any consecutive 12-month measurement, with a sliding scale (50%–60% -> 25% credit, <50% -> 40% credit) to avoid large churn risk.
- Mid-year true-up: permit a single mid-year true-up (60 days before renewal anniversary) plus annual reconciliation. Additional true-ups add operational complexity we prefer to avoid.
- Refund payout: credits to future invoices or annual cash refund for enterprise customers upon explicit election.

I’ll also propose a conservative schedule for ramp credits: 25% credit on incremental usage above baseline in Q1 post-signature, stepping down by 10% each subsequent quarter (i.e., Q2 15%, Q3 5%). This rewards early growth while limiting long tail exposure.

If Marissa is comfortable, we can bump discount on the 36-month to 10% off list for an up-front annual prepay cadence and lock the cap. That should meet finance halfway.

-Rishi
Head of Sales Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@cloudcraft.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing concerns and options

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and Logan/Rishi for the options. Quick commercial note from my side: we can commit to the following, contingent on a 36-month signed MSA and annual prepay election by CloudCraft:

- 10% off our then-current published unit price for 36 months (price lock)
- Contractual per-unit price cap = current list price + 0% (no inflation pass-through)
- Annual prepay with optional single mid-year true-up (finance elects either credits or cash refund in year 1; afterward credits only)
- Partial refund schedule: if annualized usage <50% of committed, CloudCraft may elect a one-time refund equal to 40% of unused prepay balance in year 1; years 2–3 limited to credit only
- Ramp credit: 25% on incremental usage above baseline in Q1; 15% Q2; 5% Q3; none thereafter

I attached an updated term sheet reflecting these points (LockAndFlex_TermSheet_v2.pdf). This is our best balance between price protection for CloudCraft and predictability for Redwood’s capacity planning.

If you confirm this model, we’ll instruct legal to prepare a redline-friendly MSA and commercial appendix and we’ll get procurement contact details for PO issuance. Timeline note: to honor these terms, we need a signed LOI/PO by 2027-06-15 to lock the quoted pricing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
